text: Formula calculation typically relies evaluating measured isotopic pattern   precursor score candidates. algorithms (currently GenForm) penalize candidates   mass peaks present MS1 spectra contribute isotopic pattern. Since spectra   typically 'noisy' due background co-eluting ions, additional filtering step may recommended prior   formula calculation. precursor isolation step mass peaks removed (1)   precursor (2) likely isotopologue precursor. determine potential isotopic peaks   following parameters used:  maxIsotopes maximum number isotopes consider. instance, value 5 means   M+0 (.e. monoisotopic peak) till M+5 considered. mass peaks outside range   removed. mzDefectRange two-sized vector specifying minimum (can negative) maximum   m/z defect deviation compared precursor m/z defect. chlorinated, brominated   compounds strong m/z defect isotopologues considered higher range may desired.   hand, natural compounds range may tightened. Note search range propegated   increasing distance precursor, e.g. search range doubled M+2, tripled   M+3 etc. intRange two-sized vector specifying minimum maximum relative intensity range   compared precursor. instance, c(0.001, 2) removes peaks intensity 0.1%   200% precursor. z z value (.e. absolute charge) considerd. instance, value 2   look M+0.5, M+1 etc. Note mzDefectRange adjusted accordingly   (e.g. halved z=2). maxGap maximum number missing adjacent isotopic peaks ('gaps'). (rounded) m/z   difference previous peak exceeds value next peaks removed. Similar   z, maximum gap automatically adjusted charge. parameters list passed isolatePrec argument filter.   default values can obtained getDefIsolatePrecParams function: maxIsotopes=5; mzDefectRange=c(-0.01, 0.01); intRange=c(0.001, 2); z=1; maxGap=2

"bin": uses simple binning approach cluster data points. hclust method may give accurate results default prior patRoon 3.0, computationally demanding generally unsuitable IMS workflows due excessive use RAM. distance_* methods now default suit cases. window parameter defines clustering tolerance. method="hclust" corresponds cluster height, method="distance_*" methods value sets maximum distance compared data method="bin" corresponds bin width. small windows prevent clustering close data points (e.g. resulting split mass peaks averaged spectra), whereas big windows may cluster unrelated data points together (e.g. resulting mass inaccuracies).

code: # example data from patRoonData package dataDir <- patRoonData::exampleDataPath() anaInfo <- generateAnalysisInfo(dataDir) anaInfo <- anaInfo[1:2, ] # only focus on first two analyses (e.g. training set)  # optimize mzPPM and chromFWHM parameters ftOpt <- optimizeFeatureFinding(anaInfo, "openms", list(mzPPM = c(5, 10), chromFWHM = c(4, 8)))  # optimize chromFWHM and isotopeFilteringModel (a qualitative parameter) ftOpt2 <- optimizeFeatureFinding(anaInfo, "openms",                                  list(isotopeFilteringModel = "metabolites (5% RMS)"),                                  list(isotopeFilteringModel = "metabolites (2% RMS)"),                                  templateParams = list(chromFWHM = c(4, 8)))  # perform grouping optimization with optimized features object fgOpt <- optimizeFeatureGrouping(optimizedObject(ftOpt), "xcms",                                  list(groupArgs = list(bw = c(22, 28)),                                       retcorArgs = list(method = "obiwarp")))  # same, but using the XCMS3 interface fgOpt2 <- optimizeFeatureGrouping(optimizedObject(ftOpt), "xcms3",                                   list(groupMethod = "density", groupParams = list(bw = c(22, 28)),                                        retAlignMethod = "obiwarp"))   # plot contour of first parameter set/DoE iteration plot(ftOpt, paramSet = 1, DoEIteration = 1, type = "contour")  # generate parameter set with some predefined and custom parameters to be # optimized. pSet <- generateFeatureOptPSet("openms", chromSNR = c(3, 9),                                useSmoothedInts = FALSE)

Several filters available eliminate EICs likely devoid signal interest. original peak detection algorithm optimized can exchanged others: see     getDefPeakParams details. Data suspects MS2 precursors used pre-filter EICs, can also used filter final     feature list. [exist[=mv]] [m=<number>] [ion=-e|+e|-H|+H|+Na] [cha=<number>]         [ppm=<number>] [msmv=ndp|nsse|nsae] [acc=<number>] [rej=<number>]         [thms=<number>] [thmsms=<number>] [thcomb=<number>]         [sort[=ppm|msmv|msmsmv|combmv]] [el=<elements> [oc]] [ff=<fuzzy formula>]         [vsp[=<even|odd>]] [vsm2mv[=<value>]] [vsm2ap2[=<value>]] [hcf] [kfer[=ex]]         [wm[=lin|sqrt|log]] [wi[=lin|sqrt|log]] [exp=<number>] [oei]         [dbeexc=<number>] [ivsm2mv=<number>] [vsm2ap2=<number>]         [oms[=<filename>]] [omsms[=<filename>]] [oclean[=<filename>]]         [analyze [loss] [intens]] [dbe] [cm] [pc] [sc] [max] Explanation:         ms      : filename of MS data (*.txt)         msms    : filename of MS/MS data (*.txt)         out     : output generated formulas         exist   : allow only molecular formulas for that at least one                   structural formula exists;overrides vsp, vsm2mv, vsm2ap2;                   argument mv enables multiple valencies for P and S         m       : experimental molecular mass (default: mass of MS basepeak)         ion     : type of ion measured (default: M+H)         ppm     : accuracy of measurement in parts per million (default: 5)         msmv    : MS match value based on normalized dot product, normalized                   sum of squared or absolute errors (default: nsae)         acc     : allowed deviation for full acceptance of MS/MS peak in ppm                   (default: 2)         rej     : allowed deviation for total rejection of MS/MS peak in ppm                   (default: 4)         thms    : threshold for the MS match value         thmsms  : threshold for the MS/MS match value         thcomb  : threshold for the combined match value         sort    : sort generated formulas according to mass deviation in ppm,                   MS match value, MS/MS match value or combined match value         el      : used chemical elements (default: CHBrClFINOPSSi)         oc      : only organic compounds, i.e. with at least one C atom         ff      : overwrites el and oc and uses fuzzy formula for limits of                   element multiplicities         het     : formulas must have at least one hetero atom         vsp     : valency sum parity (even for graphical formulas)         vsm2mv  : lower bound for valency sum - 2 * maximum valency                   (>=0 for graphical formulas)         vsm2ap2 : lower bound for valency sum - 2 * number of atoms + 2                   (>=0 for graphical connected formulas)         hcf     : apply Heuerding-Clerc filter         kfer    : apply Kind-Fiehn element ratio (extended) ranges         wm      : m/z weighting for MS/MS match value         wi      : intensity weighting for MS/MS match value         exp     : exponent used, when wi is set to log         oei     : allow odd electron ions for explaining MS/MS peaks         dbeexc  : excess of double bond equivalent for ions         ivsm2mv : lower bound for valency sum - 2 * maximum valency                   for fragment ions         ivsm2ap2: lower bound for valency sum - 2 * number of atoms + 2                   for fragment ions         oms     : write scaled MS peaks to output         omsms   : write weighted MS/MS peaks to output         oclean  : write explained MS/MS peaks to output         analyze : write explanations for MS/MS peaks to output         loss    : for analyzing MS/MS peaks write losses instead of fragments         intens  : write intensities of MS/MS peaks to output         dbe     : write double bond equivalents to output         cm      : write calculated ion masses to output         pc      : output match values in percent         sc      : strip calculated isotope distributions         noref   : hide the reference information         max     : maximum number of final candidates (0 is no limit)

text: following parameters exist configure CCS calculation: method CCS calculation method. "bruker", "mason-schamp_k",   "mason-schamp_1/k" "agilent". See details . defaultCharge default charge ions. used charge information available. temperature,massGas temperature (Kelvin) exact mass drift gas. See calculation   details . MasonSchampConstant Mason-Schamp constant. See calculation details . calibrant method="agilent": calibrant data used CCS calculation.   either path Agilent .d file. path OverrideImsCal.xml file (found sample.d/AcqData). named list elements massGas, TFix beta. CCS calculation depends method parameter: bruker: uses Bruker TDF-SDK calculations. See msdata configuration   options. applicable TIMS data. mason-schamp_k: uses Mason-Schamp equation:     $$CCS = C \cdot \frac{charge}{\sqrt{u \cdot T}} \cdot \frac{1}{mobility}$$ C Mason-Schamp constant, can changed setting MasonSchampConstant parameter.       See (George et al. 2024)  details. u reduced mass drift gas ion:       $$u = \frac{m_{gas} \cdot m_{ion}}{m_{gas} + m_{ion}}$$       mass drift gas defined massGas parameter. T temperature (Kelvin) defined temperature parameter. mason-schamp_1/k: mason-schamp_k assuming inversed mobility (\(\frac{1}{k}\)).   meant TIMS data. Compared method="bruker", rely TDF-SDK may   produce results minor differences (George et al. 2024) . agilent: uses Agilent calibration data following equation: $$CCS = (mobility - t_{fix}) \cdot \frac{charge}{\beta} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{m_{ion}}{m_{ion} + m_{gas}}}}$$ \(t_{fix}\) \(\beta\) TFix beta values calibration data.     massGas parameter sets \(m_{gas}\) value. getCCSParams function generates parameter list defaults.
